metrics.label: Brent crude
metrics.blurb: The global benchmark price for crude oil. Most oil cargoes price off it.

metrics.label: WTI crude
metrics.blurb: The US crude benchmark. Its gap to Brent drives US export volumes.

metrics.label: Dutch TTF gas
metrics.blurb: Europe's benchmark gas price, set in the Netherlands.

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas
metrics.blurb: The US benchmark gas price, set in Louisiana.

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)
metrics.blurb: Price of coal delivered into northwest Europe. A dry bulk demand signal.
metrics.no_free_source: API2 coal is an Argus/McCloskey assessment and is not published free.

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil
metrics.blurb: A refined product price that tracks what bunker fuel costs.
metrics.no_free_source: Refined product futures are exchange-licensed; no free daily source.

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline
metrics.blurb: US gasoline price. Strong margins here pull product tankers west.
metrics.no_free_source: Refined product futures are exchange-licensed; no free daily source.

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding dry bulk freight futures. A rough daily read on bulker sentiment.

metrics.label: Tanker ETF (BWET)
metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: Aframax (TD7, N.Sea→UKC)

brief.text:
The standout in today's data is that crude fell hard while tanker earnings stayed at extraordinary levels. Brent, the main North Sea crude benchmark, dropped 5.02 dollars to 123.10 per barrel, a 3.9 percent fall, and WTI, its US equivalent, fell 1.88 to 103.37. Yet VLCC earnings on TD3C, the Arabian Gulf to China route for the largest crude tankers, are shown at 1,287,851 US dollars per day on a time-charter-equivalent basis, which is the daily profit left to an owner after voyage costs. Suezmax on TD20 (West Africa to UK Continent) is 406,769 and Aframax on TD7 (North Sea to UK Continent) 481,500. For anyone fixing crude tonnage, the cost of oil and the cost of moving it are plainly disconnected right now. The data here does not show why Brent fell today.

On other prices, US gas at Henry Hub rose 9.5 percent to 2.76 dollars per mmBtu, while Dutch TTF gas is shown at 96.29 euros per MWh with no change figure. Bunker fuel, the ship's own fuel, rose everywhere: VLSFO Singapore 1,019.50 dollars a tonne (up 17.50), Rotterdam 794.50 (up 16.50), Fujairah 993.50 (up 9.50), Houston 850.50 (up 13.00). The Baltic Dry Index, which tracks dry bulk freight, was almost flat at 2,714, up 2 points. Panamax at 1,889 and Supramax at 1,865 have no change data; the Capesize index figure of 3,726 is stale and is not today's number. Clean product rates split sharply: MR Rotterdam–New York just 12,900 dollars a day against US Gulf–UK Continent at 53,900. LNG rates are firm, BLNG3 US Gulf to Japan at 58,900, and one headline notes "Atlantic and Pacific LNG rates continue to rise".

Running stories: no new headline today develops the Hormuz hull attacks, the Black Sea drone strikes, the US blacklist or the Russian diesel-to-America trade, so treat all four as unchanged rather than resolved. One commentary piece does refer to "the closure of Hormuz" and Gulf crude moving "around the Stra[it]", which may reflect continuing disruption there.

Watch two things. First, port labour: a strike threat at Los Angeles and Long Beach has been delayed as talks extend, while dockworkers struck across Europe over arms shipments on Friday. Second, bunker prices rising while crude falls, which squeezes voyage economics independently of oil.

storylines.title: Direct attacks on ships in Hormuz
storylines.what: A tanker caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after explosives were attached to its hull, reported as a new method of attack against commercial shipping, with multiple incidents reported. Gulf oil producers are said to be assembling nearly 230 tankers to keep crude moving through the strait amid owner reluctance.
storylines.why_it_matters: Limpet-style attacks on hulls raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for ships transiting Hormuz, shrinking the pool of owners willing to lift Arabian Gulf cargoes and feeding into already extreme VLCC and Suezmax earnings.
storylines.latest: No new incident reported today; commentary refers to Gulf crude having 'rambled on around the Stra[it]' following 'the closure of Hormuz'.
sources: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?

storylines.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea this month that have raised concerns about a widening conflict.
storylines.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure in the Black Sea threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
storylines.latest: No new Black Sea incident in today's data; European dockworkers struck partly over 'the number of seafarers killed in wars from the Gulf to the Black Sea'.
sources: Dockworkers Strike Continues Friday Against Arms Shipments

storylines.title: US Iran blockade warnings and vessel blacklist
storylines.what: US forces have reiterated blockade warnings to shipping, with the PGSA blacklist expanding to 125 vessels, alongside a piracy warning for the Gulf of Aden.
storylines.why_it_matters: A growing blacklist shrinks the compliant tanker pool and raises war-risk and routing costs through Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, which feeds directly into crude and product tanker earnings.
sources: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz recorded six VLCC transits on Oct 25, the most since Oct 17, while Bab al-Mandab recorded one VLCC on each of Oct 24 and Oct 25. Vessel waiting remains elevated across the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, with 265 dry bulk vessels waiting as of 28 October and Fujairah holding 28% of them.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times are a direct read on whether ships are routing through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
storylines.latest: No new transit counts today; VLCC TD3C TCE stands at 1,287,851 USD/day and Suezmax TD20 at 406,769 USD/day.
sources: Ramble On: Who Pays the Freight?

storylines.title: Russian diesel returning across the Atlantic
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market is said to be creating a new trade, but it has run into political opposition, with pushback reported to be gaining traction among US energy importers.
storylines.why_it_matters: A reopened Atlantic diesel route would reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns, but political and legal resistance leaves the trade uncertain.
sources: Russian LNG production up 15.2 percent in January-September

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A strike threatening major US container terminals at Los Angeles and Long Beach has been postponed while the Pacific Maritime Association and the ILWU extend talks, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond on Friday in protest at arms shipments through their ports.
storylines.why_it_matters: Simultaneous labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and an unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to future stoppages.
storylines.latest: New story: US West Coast strike delayed as talks extend; European dockworker strike continued Friday, disrupting shipping and ferries.
sources: Strike Threat at Los Angeles, Long Beach Ports Delayed as Union and Employers Extend Talks

sources: Russian LNG production up 15.2 percent in January-September

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A strike threatening major US container terminals at Los Angeles and Long Beach has been postponed while the Pacific Maritime Association and the ILWU extend talks, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond on Friday in protest at arms shipments through their ports.
storylines.why_it_matters: Simultaneous labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and an unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to future stoppages.
storylines.latest: New story: US West Coast strike delayed as talks extend; European dockworker strike continued Friday, disrupting shipping and ferries.
sources: Strike Threat at Los Angeles, Long Beach Ports Delayed as Union and Employers Extend Talks
Dockworkers Strike Continues Friday Against Arms Shipments
